title: Pinned pixel-world checkout and alpha contract — first execution
verdict: PASS. A composition frame is checked out of a live After Effects through the AEGP render path on the host callback thread, and the alpha contract is settled by measurement: AE's world is natively ARGB, AEGP_MatteMode_PREMUL_BLACK produces premultiplied pixels that are byte-for-byte identical to an independently exported Render Queue reference, and AEGP_MatteMode_STRAIGHT differs exactly where it must. One serious trap found: requesting a non-native channel order corrupts repeat checkouts.

environment.host: After Effects 2026 (26.3), Windows, vendored SDK ae25.6_61
suites: AEGP Render Suite v5 (kAEGPRenderSuiteVersion5, whose value is 8)

proven: A frame is checked out and checked back in with no error: AEGP_CheckinFrame returned 0 on every call.
The render runs on the adapter's own hook thread: threadId equalled the thread recorded at the first idle tick, so onHookThread was true for every checkout. Nothing touched a worker thread.
Geometry is exact and unpadded at every depth: 8-bit rowBytes 7680, 16-bit 15360, 32-bit 30720, each exactly width x bytesPerPixel, so rowPadding was 0 throughout.
All three world types are real: AEGP_SetWorldType(8|16|32) was honoured and the matching type-specific base address returned a payload of 8,294,400 / 16,588,800 / 33,177,600 bytes.
Both matte modes and both channel orders were accepted by AEGP_SetMatteMode and AEGP_SetChannelOrder; none was refused.
The checkout is deterministic: two consecutive checkouts of one unchanged frame produced identical pixel digests.

Byte-for-byte agreement with the independent reference: the 8-bit payload equals the Render Queue TIFF's strip payload exactly — 8,294,400 bytes, zero differing bytes, pixel SHA-256 788ae0147bdf979a6575938ca2d7d440 on both sides.
Frame-to-time conversion uses AEGP_GetCompFrameDuration as an exact rational, so a 30000/1001 composition cannot drift off frame boundaries.

findings.finding: AEGP_NewFromItem inherits the composition's *current* render options, including the Composition panel's downsample factor. The very first checkout returned 480x270 for a 1920x1080 composition because the panel sat at quarter resolution.
findings.consequence: Resolution must be stated, never inherited: the adapter now calls AEGP_SetDownsampleFactor(1,1) and AEGP_SetRenderQuality(BEST) on every checkout. Without it a pixel gate would fail — or silently pass — on an operator's zoom level.
findings.severity: would have invalidated every comparison in this phase

findings.finding: A frame index far beyond the composition's duration is not refused. Requesting frame 99999 of a 3600-frame composition returned A_Err_NONE and a full 1920x1080 frame.
findings.consequence: Range checking belongs to the caller. A runtime that trusts After Effects to reject an out-of-range request will silently present clamped pixels as the frame it asked for — so AE-F2's frame path must validate the index against the composition before it asks.

findings.finding: Byte-level alpha reasoning does not survive a change of depth. A first version derived the packed row from a hardcoded 4 bytes per pixel and reported a correct 16-bit row as half padding.
findings.consequence: Stride comes from the world type, and the 16- and 32-bit payloads are written while their alpha statistics are reported as unavailable rather than computed with 8-bit assumptions.

findings.finding: Requesting a non-native channel order corrupts repeat checkouts. With AEGP_SetChannelOrder(BGRA), consecutive checkouts of the same unchanged frame alternate between BGRA and ARGB layout: five identical requests returned BGRA, ARGB, BGRA, ARGB, BGRA. The flip follows the number of calls, not the request — alternating the requested order produced the same alternation, and changing the frame did not stop it. Requesting the native ARGB order is stable across repeats.
findings.mechanism: [INFERENCE] The swizzle appears to be applied in place to After Effects' cached world, so each checkout re-swizzles a buffer that was already swizzled. The measurements are direct; this explanation of them is not.
findings.consequence: A runtime that asks for BGRA gets correct pixels on odd calls and channel-swapped pixels on even ones — a defect that would pass a single-frame test and then corrupt live output. GrapiX must request ARGB and perform its own swizzle to the BGRA8 consumer contract. AE-F1's ring descriptor must therefore carry the observed layout, not the requested one.

notProvenYet: 16-bit and 32-bit agreement against a reference: no 16/32-bit reference has been exported yet.

World lifetime after check-in. The SDK states the world is read-only and not owned by the plugin; that contract was respected rather than tested, because testing it means reading freed memory inside the host.
Cancellation: AEGP_RenderAndCheckoutFrame was called with a null cancel function, so the cancel path is unexercised.
Any frame that costs real time. Every render here reported 0-16 ms because the frames are empty, so no timing or deadline claim can be made.
Whether the channel-order toggle also affects 16- and 32-bit worlds, and whether forcing a fresh render defeats it. Only the 8-bit path was measured.
Antialiased and gradient edges, coloured translucent shadows, and premultiplied-black edge cases: the probe covers opaque, uniform 50% and zero alpha only. The wider corpus is BO0a's.

alphaObserved.note: A fully transparent frame satisfies the premultiplied invariant trivially. It is evidence of geometry and of the zero-alpha case, and evidence of nothing else.

fixture.authoredBy: the adapter's own `fixture` verb, because this repository's .aep files are parser fixtures whose layers carry no renderable source — every frame they render is uniformly transparent, and every alpha hypothesis fits that equally well

regions.topLeft: 320x180 pure red solid at 100% opacity — opaque, and identifies the red channel
regions.topRight: 320x180 pure green solid at 50% opacity — the decisive case: green must be ~128 if premultiplied and 255 if straight

proven.nativeChannelOrder: ARGB, matching PF_Pixel {alpha, red, green, blue}. Five consecutive checkouts requesting ARGB returned channelMax [255,255,128,0] every time.
proven.premultipliedRequest: premul-black: the 50% quadrant reads A=128 G=128, and zero pixels in the frame carry a colour channel above their alpha (colourAboveAlpha 0).
proven.straightRequest: straight: the same quadrant reads A=128 G=255, and exactly 57,600 pixels — the quadrant's pixel count — carry colour above alpha, worst excess 127.
proven.referenceAgreement: The premul-black checkout, mapped ARGB->RGBA, is byte-for-byte identical to the aerender TIFF: 921,600 bytes, zero differing bytes. The straight checkout differs on exactly 57,600 bytes with worst delta 127, so the comparison is sensitive enough for the identical result to mean something.
proven.renderQueueAlpha: After Effects' own 'TIFF Sequence with Alpha' output is PREMULTIPLIED: its 50% quadrant is [R 0, G 128, B 0, A 128]. It still declares ExtraSamples = 0, 'unspecified' — so the container's silence is not a hint that the pixels are straight.
